statement: For every real x, the convergent series Sum'_p (log (1 - 1/p) + 1/p) (value B_1 - gamma) is dominated by every finite partial sum over Nat.primesLE floor(x).
proof_summary: log (1 - 1/p) + 1/p <= 0 for every prime p, from Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos applied to 1 - 1/p.
|log (1 - 1/p) + 1/p| <= 2/p^2, from Real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le with x = 1/p and n = 1 (bound 1/(p(p-1)) <= 2/p^2).

Summability over Nat.primes by comparison with Sum 2/n^2 (Real.summable_one_div_nat_pow at p = 2), then the general lemma `a summable non-positive series is dominated by each of its finite partial sums` (Summable.sum_le_tsum on the negative, then negation).

tsum_subtype unfolds the tsum over the subtype Nat.Primes into an indicator tsum over Nat, which agrees with the target summand on Nat.primesLE floor(x) because every element there is prime (Nat.mem_primesLE).
